concept.name: Flat yield curve
concept.definition: A yield curve configuration in which yields are approximately equal across maturities, so the term spread is near zero. It typically appears as a transitional state between an upward-sloping (normal) curve and an inverted curve, or vice versa.
concept.intuition: The market is charging roughly the same rate to borrow for one year as for ten years — a sign that expectations about the future are unusually uncertain or in transition.
concept.mechanics: Identified when the spread between long- and short-maturity constant-maturity yields (e.g. 10-year minus 2-year Treasury) is close to zero; flattening occurs when short rates rise toward long rates (bear flattener) or long rates fall toward short rates (bull flattener).
concept.failure_modes: A flat curve carries little standalone signal: it can precede steepening or inversion, and 'flatness' has no precise threshold, so classification is judgment-dependent.
concept.misconceptions: A flat curve is not a neutral or 'no information' state in a predictive sense, and it is not a distinct market regime with proven consequences — it is simply a descriptive shape.
concept.example: If the 2-year Treasury yields 4.20% and the 10-year yields 4.25%, the 2s10s segment is essentially flat at 5 basis points.
